subheading: CLINICAL FEATURES OF VITAMIN A DEFICIENCY

text:
CLINICAL FEATURES OF VITAMIN A DEFICIENCY
- VAD may be asymptomatic
- Increased risk of respiratory and diarrhoeal infections
- Decreased growth rate
- Retarded bone development
- Increased fatigue as a manifestation of VAD anaemia
- Bitot spots
- Poor dark adaptation (nyctalopia)
- Dry skin, Dry hair, pruritus, broken fingernails, Keratomalacia
- Xerophthalmia
- Follicular hyperkeratosis (phrynoderma) from blockage of hair follicles
   with plugs of keratin
- Excessive deposition of periosteal bone secondary to reduced osteoclastic
   activity
- Anaemia
- Keratinization of mucous membranes
